title: A bounded-below localization unit telescope has a strict complex model
statement: Every bounded-below derived integral coefficient object K admits a strictly bounded-below representative C, with a fixed lower bound a, and an isomorphism from Q of the colimit of the good-truncated scalar sequence of C to the canonical localization cocone vertex of K. Under this isomorphism every complex cocone leg equals the corresponding derived localization leg after the representative isomorphism. Definitions and notation: [def-weil-pbc-integral-localization-telescope], [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity].

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), referring to Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.2; scalar localization telescope

proof.text: Choose a representative C strictly zero below a using the standard bounded-below derived representative theorem. Its good truncation below a is an isomorphism, so reindexing and the universal property identify its good-truncated telescope colimit with its ordinary complex telescope colimit.

Use the termwise/derived unit comparison and unit naturality under the representative isomorphism. The resulting vertex isomorphism commutes with the zeroth leg; invertibility of ℓ and leg determination give every leg. Scalar invertibility reuses the existing module_nsmul_isIso or derived_nsmul_isIso theorem from ContinuousConstructibleIntegralImage, made public without changing its type or proof.
